claims.label: CERCLA Cost Recovery
claims.note: Liability is strict/joint/several once PRP status attaches -- allocation share is the real question, not whether liability exists at all. Because this plaintiff is itself a PRP (owner operator) rather than a qualifying Sec. 107(b) innocent landowner (Advanced Tech. Corp. v. Eliskim, Inc., No. 1:96CV755 (N.D. Ohio 2000)), it is functionally limited to a contribution-style claim -- recovering only the OTHER parties' equitable share, not the full cost -- modeled here in the same range as this category's own CERCLA Contribution claim.

claims.label: CERCLA Contribution (PRP vs. PRP)
claims.note: Courts apply equitable factors that typically REDUCE a mechanically-calculated share, and an unrecoverable 'orphan share' for defunct/judgment-proof historical operators is common.

outcome.description: After a 14-day bench trial the court allocated to the United States 24.67% of past response costs at the Baytown refinery ($45,567,403 in stipulated past costs), 36.54% at the Baytown Ordnance Works/Tankfarm 3000 Area ($5,481,340) and 14.4% at the Baton Rouge refinery ($26,046,130), compared with Exxon's proposed 29.67%, 36.54% and 19.4% and the government's proposed 2.36%, 1.86% and 0.46%. It held no offset for Exxon's roughly $269 million insurance settlement was warranted because there was no double recovery, and declared the same shares apply to future costs. The total damage award in Exxon's favor was $20,328,670, which is $16,994,815 in allocated past costs plus $3,333,855 in accrued prejudgment interest. The outcome amount is that stated total, interest included.
outcome.finalNote: Trial judgment; appeal status could not be verified, so the final figure is pending.
